answer: A per-round sequential proof makes each identity pay in wall-clock time: every account must forge a memory-hard hash chain of about 4 minutes over 2 GB, seeded by the jade beacon that opens each epoch, so it cannot be precomputed. Steps cannot be parallelized, so 1,000 sybils need 1,000 machines running at once, roughly 2 TB of RAM per round, while an honest agent spends one core for minutes. Verifiers spot-check links; a bad link burns the stake. Colluders cannot pool one machine, since the ivory registry binds each chain to its own key.
